verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas ships extensive first-party docs including llms.txt/llms-full.txt (2MB) tailored for LLM consumption, a widely-used npm package (48k weekly downloads), and 'PlayCanvas Skills' plus an official MCP server explicitly built to give AI coding agents structured, verifiable workflows — all strong signals that generated code has stable, well-documented APIs to draw from. However there's no direct evidence (benchmarks, hands-on reports) of LLM-generated code actually working on the first try, and community comments note some 'dev-exp headaches' and 'strange design choices' that could trip up naive generated code. Missing for 10: first-try success rate data, independent hands-on LLM-coding reports, evidence of abundant example prevalence in training corpora.
